column7: an activation with no recorded review, already older than break_glass.review_window, is counted as a deviation in the compliance posture report, together with the age of the worst outstanding one and the window it was measured against. This is exactly and only what ADR-112's every activation must be reviewed afterwards means (its own words: an open activation without a recorded review shows as a posture deviation) -- visibility, plus RunBreakGlassReviewReminder's recurring warning and audit event. A still-active unreviewed activation is counted too, since the ADR says an OPEN activation and ReviewBreakGlass refuses to review one that is still active. A pending review never blocks break-glass ACTIVATION itself (INV-CORE-break-glass-unreviewed-reported-never-blocks-activation, narrowed #2461 round 2) -- that scoping does not forbid a future, separately-decided, opt-in enforcement elsewhere
